subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth refresh succeeds but cron/heartbeat fail with 10s auth refresh timeout

question: Should OpenClaw mitigate Codex's 10s external-auth callback deadline by reusing usable cached tokens or changing refresh timing, instead of waiting for upstream Codex configurability?
rationale: The source-backed gap is real, but the permanent fix changes the product contract for when OpenClaw must force-refresh versus when it may answer Codex with existing credentials and surface a later reauth/status incident.

options.title: Mitigate in the OpenClaw bridge
options.body: Use a narrow, tested cached-token or fast-fail path for Codex app-server refresh callbacks so valid sessions do not miss the 10s upstream deadline.

options.title: Fold into broader auth incident design
options.body: Move the remaining work under the broader provider quarantine/status issues and accept that this specific timeout report stays open until that design lands.

options.title: Wait for upstream Codex
options.body: Leave OpenClaw behavior unchanged and rely on upstream Codex to make EXTERNAL_AUTH_REFRESH_TIMEOUT configurable or longer.

recommendation.title: Mitigate in the OpenClaw bridge
recommendation.body: Use a narrow, tested cached-token or fast-fail path for Codex app-server refresh callbacks so valid sessions do not miss the 10s upstream deadline.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans Codex app-server runtime, auth refresh policy, and operator-facing recovery, where recent history shows strong adjacent ownership and PR 100713 merge involvement.
